question.prompt:
In the adjoining figure of a rectangular solid, \(\angle DHG=45^\circ\) and \(\angle FHB=60^\circ.\) Find the cosine of \(\angle BHD.\)

[Figure 1](figures/1982_AMC_12_Q18_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The given angles lie in rectangular faces. Finding the edge proportions first will reveal an isosceles triangle containing the desired angle.

Let \(HF=t>0\). Triangle \(HFB\) is right at \(F\), so the given \(60^\circ\) angle gives
\[
FB=HF\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3\,t.
\]
The corresponding vertical edges of the rectangular solid are equal, so \(GD=FB=\sqrt3\,t\). Triangle \(HGD\) is right at \(G\). Using its \(45^\circ\) angle,
\[
\frac{GD}{HG}=\tan45^\circ=1,
\qquad HG=\sqrt3\,t.
\]
Now the Pythagorean theorem gives the two face diagonals from \(H\):
\[
HB^2=t^2+3t^2=4t^2,
\qquad
HD^2=3t^2+3t^2=6t^2.
\]
On the top rectangular face, \(BC=HF=t\) and \(CD=HG=\sqrt3\,t\). Thus
\[
BD^2=BC^2+CD^2=t^2+3t^2=4t^2.
\]
Consequently, \(HB=BD=2t\), while \(HD=\sqrt6\,t\). Triangle \(BHD\) is therefore isosceles with base \(HD\).

Let \(T\) be the midpoint of \(HD\). In an isosceles triangle, the median from the apex is also an altitude, so \(BT\perp HD\). This creates a right triangle in which we can use the adjacent-side-to-hypotenuse definition of cosine. Since \(T\) lies between \(H\) and \(D\),
\[
\cos\angle BHD
=\cos\angle BHT
=\frac{HT}{HB}
=\frac{HD/2}{HB}
=\frac{\sqrt6\,t/2}{2t}
=\frac{\sqrt6}{4}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\frac{\sqrt6}{4}}\), choice \(\boxed{D}\).
solutions.title: Face diagonals and an isosceles triangle
Use face right triangles and the cosine law in triangle BHD
